subject: Problem when deploying App that uses own data

messages.author: 0ff21f2dbdd1d7d5
messages.subject: Problem when deploying App that uses own data
parts:
Hello! I think I may have found a problem that some other windows users might encounter when trying to deploy an app that sources/loads a file from your disc. I had an app that behaved well when running locally, but it depended on loading a .Rdata file located somewhere like "C:/workingdirectory/Myapp/data/myfile.Rdata". I ran deployApp() and it went smoothly but  the app wouldn't work (it had that grayish dissapointing look). I figured it had something to do with how I was trying to load so I tried a few things with no success until I decided to add this bit of code to download the data from dropbox instead:

diputados.m<-repmis::source_DropboxData("diputados.csv","qr3scz6dwx3wyrl",sep=",",header=TRUE)
senadores.m<-repmis::source_DropboxData("senadores.csv","0dguhsu56s4umu5",sep=",",header=TRUE)

And then it worked fine, as you can see here in MYAPP. I wonder what the correct way of pathing is. I imagine is something like load("~/myusername/Shinyapps/myapp/data/myfile.Rdata") but I couldn't quite figure it out. I imagine any other windows users are gonna be confused as to why their app isn't running on the web even though locally it runs perfect and something like this might be the problem.

Cheers

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Problem when deploying App that uses own data
parts:
Hi,

You should always use a relative path name when accessing your applications data or other files. The relative path name should be from the application directory. 

In other words, if your local file is located at "C:\Documents\MyApp\mydata.csv", you should do something like this:

setwd("C:\Documents\MyApp")
runApp()
deployApp()

Inside your source files you can reference "mydata.csv" directly and it will work both remotely and locally.

-Andy
